raw_response:
I'll think through this as the farmer would, then give my plan.

---

I have been doing this for forty years. My hands know this soil. I cannot read the bags of fertilizer well, but I know what they look like and how many I carry home from the shop each season. I do what my husband and I always did, and what my neighbors in the village do. When everyone on our lane buys the same white bags at the shop, I buy the same.

My 12 mu — I keep 10 mu on the wheat-maize pattern like most everyone here. That is two harvests a year from the same ground. I keep 2 mu in cotton because my mother grew cotton and I still keep a little. But cotton is heavy work — picking, spraying, weeding — and there is only me and the old man in the house now. Two mu is all these old hands can manage. More than that and the cotton would rot in the field because we cannot pick fast enough.

**For the wheat** (October planting, June harvest): I plant the good seed the shop gives — the one everyone plants, I don't know the name but it is the improved kind. I spread **two bags of the mixed fertilizer (二铵, the compound)** before plowing — that is one bag per two mu I spread, pushing it with my hand from the sack. No, wait — I mean one bag covers about two mu, so six bags for the ten mu. Then in spring when the wheat wakes up green I scatter **urea, about half a bag per mu**. My neighbor Zhang's wife told me years ago: "if the wheat looks yellow, add more urea." I always add enough because a thin wheat crop is a hungry winter. Better to waste a little fertilizer than to short the grain. I water from the well **three times** — once before winter so the soil is not dry, once when it greens up in spring, once when the ear is filling. I spray **two times** for the bugs and the white powder disease. I expect about **nine hundred jin per mu** (450 kg) if the weather is kind.

**For the maize** (planted right after wheat, harvested October): I use the hybrid seed — everyone uses hybrid now, the old kind gives nothing. I do not plow between wheat and maize, no time, I just poke the seed in with the hand-planter. One bag of compound per two mu at planting, then a **big scoop of urea at the knee-high stage** — maybe half a bag per mu. Water **twice** — once after planting if no rain, once at tasseling. Spray **once** for the borer worm that eats the stalk. I get maybe **one thousand jin per mu** (500 kg) — the maize is stronger than the wheat here.

**For the cotton** (2 mu, planted April): Cotton eats fertilizer and eats medicine. I put **three bags of compound over the two mu** before planting and another scoop of urea when it flowers. I have to water **three times** from the well because cotton is thirsty. And the spray — ai-yo, the spray — **six or seven times** against the bollworm and the aphids. My back hurts just thinking of it. But cotton gives cash money, not just grain to eat. I expect **five hundred jin per mu** (250 kg) of seed cotton, if the worms do not eat it all.

I plow the wheat ground with the tractor man from the village — I pay him for the big plow on the wheat field. For maize I do no plowing, straight into the stubble. For cotton I have him do the rotary tiller, not the deep plow — the deep plow is expensive.
